title: High-Value Transaction Review
text: High-value financial transactions may require additional review when the amount exceeds normal customer activity or internal monitoring thresholds. Reviewers should consider transaction amount, customer profile, source of funds, destination, and recent activity. A high transaction value alone does not establish suspicious behavior, but it can increase the need for further review when combined with other risk indicators. Transactions at or above the demo monitoring threshold of 10,000 should receive enhanced review in this training system.

title: Cross-Border Transaction Review
text: Cross-border transactions should be reviewed with attention to the origin country, destination country, customer profile, payment purpose, and transaction history. International movement of funds may require additional verification when activity differs from the customer's expected behavior. Reviewers should consider whether the customer normally performs international transactions and whether other risk indicators are present.

title: Wire Transfer Monitoring
text: Wire transfers may receive enhanced monitoring because they can move funds quickly between financial institutions and jurisdictions. Review should consider the amount, sender information, beneficiary information, geographic destination, transaction frequency, and consistency with known customer behavior. High-value international wire transfers may require additional review when multiple risk indicators occur together.

title: Large Cash Withdrawal Review
text: Large cash withdrawals should be reviewed when the amount is unusual compared with the customer's normal activity. Reviewers should consider withdrawal amount, recent deposits, withdrawal frequency, customer profile, and whether several cash transactions occur within a short period. In this demo system, cash withdrawals at or above 5,000 may trigger an additional monitoring rule.

title: Customer Geographic Consistency
text: Transaction geography should be compared with the customer's registered location and historical activity. Activity originating from a country that differs from the customer's normal location may require additional review, especially when combined with high transaction value, international transfers, unusual devices, or unexpected transaction channels. Geographic differences should be treated as a risk indicator rather than automatic evidence of wrongdoing.

title: Transaction Velocity Monitoring
text: Repeated transactions occurring within a short time window can indicate unusual activity when they are inconsistent with expected customer behavior. Monitoring systems should evaluate transaction count, combined value, destinations, payment channels, and time intervals. Several transfers that appear individually normal may warrant review when their combined pattern is unusual.

title: Customer Identity and Profile Review
text: Customer information should be sufficiently complete to support transaction monitoring and risk analysis. Relevant information can include customer identity, country, business type, expected activity, and account purpose. When transaction behavior differs significantly from the established customer profile, reviewers may request additional information or perform enhanced review.

title: Risk Escalation and Manual Review
text: Transactions that trigger multiple independent risk indicators may require manual review. Reviewers should be able to understand which monitoring rules were triggered and why the system assigned a particular risk level. Automated scoring should remain explainable, and analysts should have access to the transaction information, matched rules, relevant policy guidance, and audit history before making a final decision.
